rationale: Using the remaining allocation on the one thread of this run whose account is still source-only: the StateSnapshot repair duty. The harness now forces a follower's Progress into StateSnapshot on a real leader (log compacted past the follower's next index, a storage snapshot present, the peer recently active) and then exercises both producers named in the source account. A local run records the entry state (StateSnapshot, match 1, pendingSnap 2, paused true, one message emitted) and then: a peer MsgAppResp reporting index 2 leaves the Progress in StateReplicate with match 2 and unpaused, and an application report delivered as MsgSnapStatus with Reject leaves a freshly snapshotted Progress in StateProbe with PendingSnapshot cleared to 0 while appends stay paused. That converts the source-only account into an observed one. Submitted as a fixed experiment so the controller can produce the receipt; no interpretation is added because the receipt does not exist yet.

scope.description: Measure the two producers that can move a follower's Progress out of StateSnapshot: a peer MsgAppResp reporting the snapshot applied, and an application snapshot report delivered as MsgSnapStatus.
assumptions: Real raft instances over voters {1,2,3} built with newTestRaft; the follower's Progress is placed where the leader's log no longer covers its next index by compacting memory storage to index 2 with a snapshot at index 2, then setting match 1/next 2 and RecentActive true for peer 2.
The snapshot path is entered through maybeSendAppend, the production call, so StateSnapshot is reached the way the leader reaches it in service.

For the application-driven repair a second instance is used whose peer 3 is put into StateSnapshot directly with BecomeSnapshot(1), then stepped with a rejecting MsgSnapStatus, which is how ReportSnapshot delivers a failure.
excluded: Any claim about a network partition or about snapshot transfer itself; only the leader-side Progress transitions are measured.
The case where the peer's MsgAppResp is lost entirely, which remains a source-based account.

experiment.prefix: TestAssuranceSnapshotRepair builds a memory storage with voters {1,2,3}, appends two entries, creates a snapshot at index 2 and compacts to it, then constructs a leader with newTestRaft, promotes it, and sets peer 2's Progress to match 1, next 2, RecentActive true. It calls maybeSendAppend(2,false) and emits a setup event with the log first index, whether a message was emitted, the Progress state, match, PendingSnapshot and IsPaused. It then steps a MsgAppResp from peer 2 at index 2 and emits the repair event with the resulting state, match and pause flag. Finally a second leader has peer 3 moved into StateSnapshot directly with BecomeSnapshot(1), emits a before event, and steps a rejecting MsgSnapStatus from peer 3, emitting the resulting state, PendingSnapshot and pause flag.

comparisons.description: The peer-driven repair works: an MsgAppResp that advances match past the log start puts the Progress back into StateReplicate and clears the pause.
The application-driven repair works: a rejecting MsgSnapStatus moves the Progress to StateProbe and clears PendingSnapshot, so probing resumes from the matched index.

knowledge.assertion: StateSnapshot pauses appends and has exactly two exit producers, one peer-driven and one application-driven
